summary: Two Python claims are confirmed; nine repository-specific claims are unverifiable from the permitted files and empty ledger. Public searches found no primary evidence establishing those local assertions. Their required actions concern unsupported factual wording, not demonstrated code defects. The 18-month update search found reinforcing Python 3.15 documentation without a relevant semantic change. No landscape scan was required.

claims.claim: Python 3.12 compares aware datetimes with different fixed UTC offsets by their represented instants, so 2026-09-30T17:00:01-07:00 and 2026-10-01T00:00:01Z compare equal when parsed as aware datetimes.

sources.title: datetime — Basic date and time types — Python 3.12.15 documentation
sources.quote: … the comparison acts as comparands were first converted to UTC datetimes …

sources.title: datetime — Basic date and time types — Python 3.15.0 documentation
sources.quote: … the comparison acts as comparands were first converted to UTC datetimes …

newer_practice.summary: Python 3.15.0 retains the documented comparison rule. Its official release page establishes the release date; both sources were accessed on 2026-10-10. This reinforces the claim and requires no change to this step.

claims.recommended_action: No change required. Applying the documented rule, adding seven hours to the -07:00 timestamp yields 2026-10-01T00:00:01Z. Equality follows for these aware fixed-offset datetimes.
